video_goal: Demonstrate how to create a basic cross-stitch on Aida cloth while maintaining even thread tension.
required_subjects_and_props: White Aida cloth, wooden embroidery hoop, red embroidery floss, blunt tapestry needle

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place a square of white Aida cloth evenly over the inner ring of a wooden embroidery hoop.
Hands press the outer hoop ring down over the Aida cloth, gently tugging the fabric edges to make it taut, and twist the top metal screw to tighten.
Fingers pinch the end of a strand of red embroidery floss and push it through the eye of a blunt tapestry needle.
The needle tip pokes up from beneath the taut Aida cloth, emerging cleanly through a specific bottom-left grid hole.
Fingers pull the needle and red floss upward until only a 1-inch tail remains visible underneath, holding the tail flat against the back of the cloth with an index finger.
The needle tip is inserted down into the grid hole diagonally up and to the right of the starting hole.
The thread is pulled down slowly until it lays perfectly flat against the Aida cloth grid, forming a diagonal line without puckering the surrounding fabric.
The needle emerges from the hole directly below the top-right hole, representing the bottom-right corner of the stitch square.
The needle is pushed down into the top-left hole, crossing the red floss directly over the first diagonal thread.
The thread is pulled taut to complete a perfect 'X' shape; a finger gently taps the stitch to demonstrate it is snug while the fabric grid remains perfectly square.
The hands complete two more identical 'X' stitches directly to the right of the first one, forming a uniform, evenly tensioned row of three stitches.
The hoop is flipped over to reveal the back side, and the needle is slid horizontally underneath the three vertical thread loops to secure the loose tail.
